title: Twist in the Tale
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.prompt: “Children take pleasure in giving books to each other.”

blocks.text: 這是 Matching Features。題目問的是「哪一位人物提到孩子把書送給別人或互相傳書」。定位時要找 give books、present、pass on、children social behaviour 這一組概念。
“It helps that once smitten, children are loyal and even fanatical consumers.”
有利的一點是，孩子一旦著迷，就會成為忠誠甚至狂熱的消費者。
“She has sold more than three million books, but remains virtually invisible to adults, although most ten-year-old girls know about her.”
她已售出超過三百萬本書，雖然大多數十歲女孩都知道她，但成年人幾乎看不見她的存在。
只看首尾句，可以先猜本段講兒童讀者的忠誠、消費和社交傳播，以及 Jacqueline Wilson 的銷售成功。
“They have parties—where books are a good present. If they like something, they have to pass it on.”
她們會舉辦派對，而書是很好的禮物。如果她們喜歡某樣東西，就一定要把它傳給別人。
這句來自 Jacqueline Wilson 的說法。她說自己的 average reader 是十歲女孩，並補充她們sociable and acquisitive，會 collect，會有 parties，在派對中 books are a good present。題目中的
“giving books to each other” 對應原文 “books are a good present”。
take pleasure in giving books= books are a good present to each other= parties / pass it on人物來源：整段由 “Author Jacqueline Wilson says…” 引出，所以答案是 D。
Paragraph B 也提到 book clubs，但 book clubs 只表示兒童書活動增加，沒有提到孩子互相送書。Q1 的定案詞是 present 和 pass it on。

questions.prompt: “Reading in public is an activity that children have not always felt comfortable about doing.”
questions.translation: 孩子過去未必一直覺得在公共場合閱讀是自在的事。

blocks.text: 這題要找誰提到 children being seen reading in public。定位詞是 reading in public、seen、bus、comfortable / OK。
“The main growth area has been the market for eight to fourteen-year-olds, and there is little doubt that the boom has been fuelled by the bespectacled apprentice, Harry Potter.”
主要增長區域是八至十四歲讀者市場，而且毫無疑問，這股熱潮由戴眼鏡的學徒 Harry Potter 推動。
“The current buzz around the publication of the fourth Harry Potter book beats anything in the world of adult literature.”
目前第四本 Harry Potter 出版所引起的熱潮，超越成人文學世界中的任何事情。
只看首尾句，可以估計本段講 Harry Potter 如何令兒童閱讀市場升溫。若題目談孩子是否敢在公眾面前閱讀，答案很可能在本段中間。
“‘Harry made it OK to be seen on a bus reading a book,’ says Cooling. ‘To a child, that is important.’”
Cooling 說：「Harry 令人在巴士上被看見讀書變得可以接受。對孩子來說，這很重要。」
“made it OK” 表示原本未必 OK，現在變得可以接受。題目說 children have not always felt comfortable about reading in public，正好是從 “made it OK to be seen on a bus reading a book”
reading in public= seen on a bus reading a book have not always felt comfortable= Harry made it OK人物來源：引文後面清楚寫 “says Cooling”，即 Wendy Cooling。答案是 A。
Harry Potter 是 fictional character，不是選項人物。題目要配對的是說話者，所以要看 reporting phrase “says Cooling”。

questions.prompt: “Some well-known writers of adult literature regret that they earn less than popular children’s writers.”
questions.translation: 一些著名成人文學作家會羨慕或懊惱自己賺得比受歡迎兒童作家少。

blocks.text: 這題要找 adult writers、sales 或 earnings 的比較。定位詞是 adult writers、sales、children’s writers。
“No longer are children’s authors considered mere sentimentalists or failed adult writers.”
兒童作家不再被視為單純的感傷主義者或失敗的成人作家。

“And advances seem to be growing too: UK publishing outfit Orion recently negotiated a six-figure sum from US company Scholastic for The Seeing Stone, a children’s novel by Kevin Crossley-Holland, the majority of which will go to the author.”
預付款似乎也在上升：英國出版機構 Orion 最近為 Kevin Crossley-Holland 的兒童小說 The Seeing Stone，從美國 Scholastic 談得一筆六位數金額，其中大部分會給作者。
只看首尾句，可以看出本段講兒童作家地位和收入上升，這和成人作家比較收入的題目很吻合。
“‘Some feted adult writers would kill for the sales,’ says Almond, who sold 42,392 copies of Skellig in 1999 alone.”
Almond 說：「一些備受推崇的成人作家會非常想要這種銷量。」他自己的 Skellig 單在 1999 年就售出 42,392 本。
“feted adult writers” 指受人讚賞、有名氣的成人作家。“would kill for the sales” 是誇張說法，意思是非常渴望擁有這種銷量。題目把 “sales” 轉成 “earn less”，因為在出版語境中銷量高通常帶來更高收入和更大市場價值。

well-known writers of adult literature= feted adult writers regret / envy= would kill for earn less than popular children’s writers= would kill for the sales of children’s authors人物來源：引文後寫 “says Almond”，所以答案是 B。
題目用 “earn less” 不等於原文逐字寫 income lower。這裡是根據 sales 和 advances 的上下文作合理改寫，尤其本段最後又提到 six-figure sum。

questions.prompt: “Children are quick to decide whether they like or dislike a book.”
questions.translation: 孩子會很快決定自己喜不喜歡一本書。

blocks.text: 要找誰說孩子很快放棄一本書。定位詞是 quick decide、like or dislike、drop it、two pages。
“‘A few years ago, publishers lost confidence and wanted to make books more like television, the medium that frightened them most,’ says children’s book critic Julia Eccleshare.”
兒童書評論家 Julia Eccleshare 說：「幾年前，出版社失去信心，想把書變得更像它們最害怕的媒介——電視。」最後一句：
“‘If they don’t get it in two pages, they’ll drop it.’”
「如果孩子在兩頁之內抓不到它的吸引力，他們就會放下它。」只看首尾句，可以看出本段講 Julia Eccleshare 對兒童閱讀的看法，尤其強調孩子讀書時判斷很快。
“Children are demanding readers,” she says. “If they don’t get it in two pages, they’ll drop it.”
她說：「孩子是要求很高的讀者。如果他們在兩頁之內抓不到它的吸引力，他們就會放下它。」
“in two pages” 是時間和速度訊號，表示孩子很快作出判斷。“drop it” 表示停止閱讀，反映他們不喜歡或不被吸引。題目用 “decide whether they like or dislike” 概括原文中的 demanding readers和 drop it。
quick to decide= in two pages dislike a book= drop it人物來源：這段第一句已點名 Julia Eccleshare，後面 “she says” 延續同一位說話者。答案是 C。
Paragraph D 的 Almond 也說孩子會問 sophisticated questions，但那是說孩子能深入閱讀；Q4問的是孩子判斷一本書是否吸引的速度，證據在 Paragraph E。

questions.prompt: “Children will read many books by an author that they like.”
questions.translation: 孩子如果喜歡某位作者，會讀那位作者的很多本書。

blocks.text: 這題要找 loyalty、fanatical consumers、collect 這一組概念。題目沒有直接說 sales，所以不能只找銷量；要找孩子對作者的持續追隨。
“It helps that once smitten, children are loyal and even fanatical consumers.”
有利的一點是，孩子一旦著迷，就會成為忠誠甚至狂熱的消費者。
“She has sold more than three million books, but remains virtually invisible to adults, although most ten-year-old girls know about her.”
她已售出超過三百萬本書，雖然對成年人幾乎看不見，但大多數十歲女孩都知道她。
只看首尾句，可以判斷本段講孩子對喜愛作者的忠誠和 Jacqueline Wilson 的強大兒童讀者群。
“It helps that once smitten, children are loyal and even fanatical consumers.”
孩子一旦著迷，就會成為忠誠甚至狂熱的消費者。
她們愛社交，也喜歡收集。她們會收集。
“once smitten” 表示一旦喜歡上。“loyal and even fanatical consumers” 表示會持續追隨和購買。“They collect” 更直接支援「會讀很多本」或「會收集同一作者的書」這個概念。
author that they like= once smitten read many books= loyal / fanatical consumers / collect人物來源：“Author Jacqueline Wilson says…” 引出本段。答案是 D。
本題和 Q1 都在 Paragraph G，都屬於 Jacqueline Wilson。Q1 抓的是送書和傳播；Q5 抓的是忠誠和收集。兩題證據相鄰，但控制點不同。

questions.prompt: “The public do not realise how much children read today.”
questions.translation: 大眾沒有意識到今天孩子其實讀得很多。

blocks.text: 這題要找 public misconception。定位詞是 public、children don’t read nowadays、truth。
“‘People still tell me, “Children don’t read nowadays”,’ says David Almond, the award-winning author of children’s books such as Skellig.”
得獎兒童作家 David Almond 說：「人們仍然告訴我：『現在的孩子不閱讀。』」最後一句：

“No one is denying that books are competing with other forms of entertainment for children’s attention, but it seems as though children find a special kind of mental nourishment within the printed page.”
沒有人否認書本要和其他娛樂形式爭奪孩子的注意力，但孩子似乎在印刷頁面中找到一種特殊的精神滋養。
首尾句顯示本段會反駁「孩子不讀書」的流行看法，這與題目完全對應。
“People still tell me, ‘Children don’t read nowadays,’ says David Almond…”
David Almond 說，人們仍然告訴他：「現在的孩子不閱讀。」再看：
“The truth is that they are skilled, creative readers.”
真相是，他們是有技巧、有創意的讀者。
“People still tell me” 對應題目中的 public。“Children don’t read nowadays” 是大眾誤解。Almond用 “The truth is…” 反駁，指出孩子其實是 skilled, creative readers，並會問 sophisticated questions。
public do not realise= People still tell me “Children don’t read nowadays”
how much children read today= The truth is that they are skilled, creative readers人物來源：句中直接寫 “says David Almond”。答案是 B。
Paragraph A 也有調查數字，說孩子每週平均讀四小時。可是 Q6 問的是哪一位人物指出大眾誤解，真正人物證據在 David Almond 的引文。

questions.prompt: “We are experiencing a rise in the popularity of children’s literature.”
questions.translation: 兒童文學的受歡迎程度正在上升。

blocks.text: 這題要找 rise / popularity / buzz / sales good / fertile period。定位詞是 popularity、children’s literature、rise。
“Moreover, the children’s book market, which traditionally was seen as a poor cousin to the more lucrative and successful adult market, has come into its own.”
此外，兒童書市場過去傳統上被視為比更有利可圖、更成功的成人市場低一等，如今已經有了自己的地位。
“‘There’s a real buzz around them. Book clubs are happening, sales are good, and people are much more willing to listen to children’s authors.’”
「它們周圍有真正的熱度。讀書會正在出現，銷售很好，人們也更願意聽兒童作家的聲音。」首尾句顯示本段講兒童書市場地位上升和人氣上升。
“‘Children’s books are going through an incredibly fertile period,’ says Wendy Cooling, a children’s literature consultant.”
兒童文學顧問 Wendy Cooling 說：「兒童書正經歷一個極其豐盛的時期。」再看：
“There’s a real buzz around them. Book clubs are happening, sales are good…”
它們正有真正的熱度。讀書會正在出現，銷售很好……
“incredibly fertile period” 表示一個創作、銷售和市場活力都很旺盛的階段。“real buzz” 和 “sales are good” 直接支援 popularity rising。
rise in popularity= real buzz / sales are good / people more willing to listen children’s literature= children’s books人物來源：引文後面寫 “says Wendy Cooling”。答案是 A。
Paragraph J 也說市場前景好，但 Q7 要配對人物；Paragraph B 直接引用 Wendy Cooling，是最準確證據。

questions.prompt: “For which age group have sales of books risen the most?”
questions.translation: 哪一個年齡組別的書本銷售增長最大？

blocks.text: 這是 Short-answer Question。題目問 age group，所以答案應該是一個年齡範圍。定位詞是sales risen the most / main growth area。
“The main growth area has been the market for eight to fourteen-year-olds, and there is little doubt that the boom has been fuelled by the bespectacled apprentice, Harry Potter.”
主要增長區域是八至十四歲讀者市場，而且毫無疑問，這股熱潮由戴眼鏡的學徒 Harry Potter 推動。
“The current buzz around the publication of the fourth Harry Potter book beats anything in the world of adult literature.”
第四本 Harry Potter 出版所引起的熱潮，超越成人文學界任何事情。
只看首尾句，已經能把答案範圍縮到 Paragraph C，因為首句直接出現 growth area 和年齡組別。
“The main growth area has been the market for eight to fourteen-year-olds…”
主要增長區域是八至十四歲讀者市場……
題目用 “sales of books risen the most” 改寫原文 “main growth area”。“market for eight to fourteen-year-olds” 指這個年齡層的兒童書市場增長最大。
答案形式： eight to fourteen-year-olds字數計算可視為三個詞：eight / to / fourteen-year-olds，符合 NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS。
sales risen the most= main growth area age group= eight to fourteen-year-olds
Paragraph A 也提到 children up to the age of 11，但那是閱讀時間調查，不是銷售增長最大年齡組別。Q8 的控制詞是 sales risen the most，對應 main growth area。

questions.prompt: “Which company has just invested heavily in an unpublished children’s book?”
questions.translation: 哪一間公司剛剛重金投資了一本尚未出版的兒童書？

blocks.text: 題目問 Which company，所以答案應是公司名稱。定位詞是 invested heavily、unpublished children’s book、company。
“No longer are children’s authors considered mere sentimentalists or failed adult writers.”
兒童作家已不再被視為單純的感傷主義者或失敗的成人作家。

“And advances seem to be growing too: UK publishing outfit Orion recently negotiated a six-figure sum from US company Scholastic for The Seeing Stone, a children’s novel by Kevin Crossley-Holland, the majority of which will go to the author.”
預付款似乎也在上升：英國出版機構 Orion 最近為 Kevin Crossley-Holland 的兒童小說 The Seeing Stone，從美國公司 Scholastic 談得一筆六位數金額，當中大部分會給作者。
只看首尾句，可以判斷本段講兒童作家收入和 advance 提升。重金投資的公司必然在末句。
“Orion recently negotiated a six-figure sum from US company Scholastic for The Seeing Stone…”
Orion 最近為 The Seeing Stone 從美國公司 Scholastic 談得一筆六位數金額……
“six-figure sum” 表示金額達六位數，即重金。這筆錢是 “from US company Scholastic”，所以投資或支付這筆巨額款項的公司是 Scholastic。題目沒有問 book title，所以不能填 The Seeing Stone。題目問 company，因此答案是 Scholastic。
invested heavily= negotiated a six-figure sum company= US company Scholastic unpublished children’s book= The Seeing Stone, a children’s novel答案形式： Scholastic = 1 word，符合字數限制。
Orion 也出現在同一句，但它是 negotiated a six-figure sum from Scholastic 的一方。題目問投入資金的公司，答案要看 from US company Scholastic。

questions.prompt: “Who is currently the best-selling children’s writer?”
questions.translation: 目前最暢銷的兒童作家是誰？

blocks.text: 這是 Who 問題，答案應是人名。定位詞是 currently、best-selling、children’s writer。
“It helps that once smitten, children are loyal and even fanatical consumers.”
孩子一旦著迷，就會成為忠誠甚至狂熱的消費者，這很有幫助。
“She has sold more than three million books, but remains virtually invisible to adults, although most ten-year-old girls know about her.”
她已售出超過三百萬本書，雖然對成年人幾乎看不見，但大多數十歲女孩都知道她。
Paragraph G 講兒童讀者忠誠和 Jacqueline Wilson 的銷量，所以 best-selling writer 的資訊在這段中間。
“After Rowling, Wilson is currently the best-selling children’s writer, and her sales have boomed over the past three years.”
在 Rowling 之後，Wilson 目前是最暢銷的兒童作家之一，而且她的銷量在過去三年急升。
這句最容易令人誤填 Wilson。關鍵在 “After Rowling”。這個短語表示 Rowling 排在 Wilson 之前。
題目問 currently the best-selling children’s writer，即最高位置的人；所以答案應填 Rowling。若答案表要求完整姓名，可用前文 Paragraph C 的 “J. K. Rowling”。
best-selling children’s writer= Rowling is the writer ahead of Wilson in sales ranking currently= currently答案形式： Rowling = 1 word；J. K. Rowling = 不超過三個詞，也符合題目限制。
Wilson 的名字和 “currently the best-selling children’s writer” 連在同一句，視覺上很吸引。判斷時要先處理句首 “After Rowling”，它把銷量排名的最前位置留給 Rowling。

questions.prompt: “the fact that children are able to identify and discuss the important elements of fiction”
questions.translation: 孩子能夠辨認並討論小說的重要元素。

blocks.text: 這是 Matching Information。題目問哪一段提到 children 能討論 fiction elements。定位詞是important elements of fiction，應預期原文出現 language、story structure、chapters、dialogue 這類詞。
“‘People still tell me, “Children don’t read nowadays”,’ says David Almond, the award-winning author of children’s books such as Skellig.”
得獎兒童作家 David Almond 說：「人們仍然告訴我：『現在的孩子不閱讀。』」最後一句：

“No one is denying that books are competing with other forms of entertainment for children’s attention, but it seems as though children find a special kind of mental nourishment within the printed page.”
沒有人否認書本要和其他娛樂形式爭奪孩子的注意力，但孩子似乎在印刷頁面中找到一種特殊的精神滋養。
只看首尾句，可以估計本段會反駁「孩子不閱讀」的說法，並證明孩子其實能深入閱讀。這和fiction elements 很相關。
“When I do classroom visits, they ask me very sophisticated questions about use of language, story structure, chapters and dialogue.”
當我到課室探訪時，他們會問我非常成熟的問題，內容涉及語言運用、故事結構、章節和對話。
use of language、story structure、chapters、dialogue 都是 fiction 的重要元素。孩子能提出sophisticated questions，表示他們不只讀故事情節，也能辨認和討論寫作技巧。
important elements of fiction= use of language, story structure, chapters and dialogue identify and discuss= ask sophisticated questions about所以答案是 Paragraph D。
Paragraph E 也談孩子是 demanding readers，但沒有列出小說元素。Q11 的定案證據是Paragraph D 中那串具體元素。

questions.translation: 兒童文化或兒童社群被低估。

blocks.text: 這是 Matching Information。題目中的 children’s society 不是指兒童組織，較接近 children’s culture。定位詞是 undervaluing、ignore、children’s culture。
“Children’s books are surprisingly relevant to contemporary life.”
兒童書出人意料地與當代生活相關。
“But Anne Fine, author of many award-winning children’s books, is concerned that the British literati still ignore children’s culture. ‘It’s considered worthy but boring,’ she says.”
但多本得獎兒童書的作者 Anne Fine 擔心，英國文學精英仍然忽視兒童文化。她說：「它被認為有價值，但沉悶。」首尾句顯示本段一方面肯定兒童書的當代相關性，另一方面指出文學圈仍低估兒童文化。
“the British literati still ignore children’s culture.”
英國文學精英仍然忽視兒童文化。
它被認為有價值，但沉悶。
“ignore children’s culture” 直接表示兒童文化未得到充分重視。“worthy but boring” 也反映一種低估：主流文學圈承認它有教育或道德價值，卻沒有把它視為真正有文學活力的文化。
children’s society= children’s culture undervaluing= ignore / considered worthy but boring所以答案是 Paragraph H。
Paragraph I 也說 children’s books should be taken more seriously as literature。可是 Q12 的“children’s society / culture” 對應最直接的是 Paragraph H 的 “children’s culture”。

questions.prompt: “the impact of a particular fictional character on the sales of children’s books”
questions.translation: 某個虛構角色對兒童書銷售的影響。

blocks.text: 題目問 particular fictional character，不是問 author。最有定位力的詞是 Harry Potter。還要找sales / boom / market growth。
“The main growth area has been the market for eight to fourteen-year-olds, and there is little doubt that the boom has been fuelled by the bespectacled apprentice, Harry Potter.”
主要增長區域是八至十四歲市場，而且毫無疑問，這股熱潮由戴眼鏡的學徒 Harry Potter 推動。
“The current buzz around the publication of the fourth Harry Potter book beats anything in the world of adult literature.”
第四本 Harry Potter 出版造成的熱潮，超越成人文學界任何事情。
只看首尾句，Paragraph C 明顯處理 Harry Potter 對兒童書市場和銷售熱潮的影響。
“the boom has been fuelled by the bespectacled apprentice, Harry Potter.”
這股熱潮由戴眼鏡的學徒 Harry Potter 推動。
“So influential has J. K. Rowling’s series of books been that they have helped to make reading fashionable for pre-teens.”
J. K. Rowling 這套書影響如此大，以至它們幫助閱讀在十來歲前的兒童之間變得時尚。
Harry Potter 是 particular fictional character。原文的 “boom has been fuelled by” 表示這個角色推動了市場熱潮。題目用 “impact on sales” 概括 “main growth area”、“boom” 和 “buzz”。
particular fictional character= Harry Potter impact on sales= boom has been fuelled by / current buzz children’s books= market for eight to fourteen-year-olds / Harry Potter book所以答案是 Paragraph C。
J. K. Rowling 是作者，Harry Potter 是角色。題目說 particular fictional character，所以定位應落在 Harry Potter，不是 Rowling 本人。

questions.prompt: “an inaccurate forecast regarding the reading habits of children”
questions.translation: 一個關於兒童閱讀習慣的不準確預測。

blocks.text: 這是 Matching Information。定位詞是 inaccurate forecast、predicting、reading habits、children.
“Less than three years ago, doom merchants were predicting that the growth in video games and the rise of the Internet would sound the death knell for children’s literature.”
不到三年前，悲觀預言者仍在預測，video games 的增長和 Internet 的興起會為兒童文學敲響喪鐘。
“A recent survey by Books Marketing found that children up to the age of 11—girls in particular—read for an average of four hours a week.”
Books Marketing 最近一項調查發現，11 歲或以下兒童，尤其是女孩，平均每週閱讀四小時。
首尾句形成明顯對比：有人預測兒童文學會死亡，但調查顯示孩子仍然閱讀不少。
“doom merchants were predicting that the growth in video games and the rise of the Internet would sound the death knell for children’s literature.”
悲觀預言者曾預測，video games 和 Internet 會令兒童文學走向死亡。
“But contrary to popular myth, children are reading more books than ever.”
但與流行迷思相反，孩子讀的書比以往更多。
“were predicting” 對應 forecast。“contrary to popular myth” 表示這個預測不準確。預測內容是兒童文學會被科技娛樂殺死；實際情況是 children are reading more books than ever。
inaccurate forecast= doom merchants were predicting… / contrary to popular myth reading habits of children= children are reading more books than ever所以答案是 Paragraph A。
文章標題下的導語也說 fears were wrong，但題目要求選 A–J 段落。A 段首句和中間句提供完整證據，因此答案填 A。

paragraphOverview.title: Skim Roadmap：先看每段首尾句建立全文地圖
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: 首句說三年前仍有人預測 video games 和 Internet 會令兒童文學走向死亡。末句引用 Books Marketing 的調查，指出 11 歲或以下兒童，尤其是女孩，每週平均閱讀四小時。只看首尾句，可以先判斷本段功能是推翻錯誤預測：科技娛樂沒有殺死兒童閱讀，實際情況剛好相反，兒童閱讀量仍然可觀。
首句說兒童書市場過去常被視為成人書市場的 poor cousin，即較不重要、利潤較低的一方。末句引用 Wendy Cooling，說兒童書有 real buzz，book clubs 正在出現，sales good，而且大眾更願意聽兒童作家的聲音。只看首尾句，可以判斷本段重點是兒童文學市場地位上升，出版社和讀者都開始重視這個領域。
首句指出主要增長區域是八至十四歲讀者市場，並說 Harry Potter 無疑推動了這個 boom。末句說第四本 Harry Potter 出版造成的 buzz，超越成人文學界任何事情。只看首尾句，可以看出本段會集中講 Harry Potter 的市場影響：它令 pre-teens 覺得閱讀變 fashionable，也帶動兒童書銷售和社會討論熱度。
首句引用 David Almond，說仍有人告訴他「現在的孩子不閱讀」。末句說兒童似乎在 printed page之中找到一種特殊的 mental nourishment。只看首尾句，可以判斷本段用 Almond 的觀察反駁大眾誤解：孩子其實是有技巧、有創意的讀者，並能深入討論語言、結構、章節和對話等小說元素。
首句引用 Julia Eccleshare，說幾年前出版社失去信心，想把書變得像它們最害怕的媒介television。末句說如果孩子在兩頁內得不到吸引，他們就會放下那本書。只看首尾句，可以判斷本段講兒童讀者的要求很高：書不應模仿電視，因為閱讀的優勢是能在腦中想像；同時，兒童很快判斷一本書是否吸引。
首句說兒童作家不再被視為 mere sentimentalists 或 failed adult writers。末句說 Orion 從美國Scholastic 為 Kevin Crossley-Holland 的兒童小說 The Seeing Stone 談得六位數金額，當中大部分會給作者。只看首尾句，可以判斷本段講兒童作家地位和收入提升：銷量、advance 和市場重視程度都已大幅提高。
首句說一旦孩子愛上一位作者，他們會成為忠誠甚至狂熱的消費者。末句說 Wilson 已售出超過三百萬本書，雖然對成年人幾乎 invisible，但大多數十歲女孩都知道她。只看首尾句，可以判斷本段講兒童讀者的社交傳播力和忠誠度：孩子會收集、送書、互相推薦，令 Jacqueline Wilson 的銷量急升。
首句說兒童書對當代生活 surprisingly relevant。末句引用 Anne Fine，說兒童文化仍被 British literati 忽視，被視為 worthy but boring。只看首尾句，可以判斷本段焦點是兒童文學的題材其實很廣，也很貼近現代生活；可是主流文學圈仍低估兒童文化，把它看得有價值但沉悶。
首句引用 Almond，說兒童書要被認真視為 literature，仍有一段路要走。末句說兒童書讓人進入神話和古老故事的寶庫，接觸 love、loss、death、redemption 等重大主題。只看首尾句，可以判斷本段延續「兒童文學仍未被充分重視」這點，同時強調兒童讀者擁有強大的 literary culture，兒童書能處理深層人類主題。
首句說目前出版界正在競逐尋找下一個 Harry Potter。末句說這對市場長遠未來和兒童作家都有好兆頭，因為兒童作家雖責任重大，過去在文學界 profile 最低。只看首尾句，可以判斷結尾段總結市場前景：出版界高度投入兒童書競標，兒童文學市場看來會繼續強勢發展。
